title: Ferrying host state without suspension: phased reintegration protocol for stateful upgrades
creator: Avery Park
description: Introduce a phased reintegration protocol that transfers essential in-memory and KV cache state from retiring hosts to replacements without globally suspending traffic. The goal is to perform stateful host upgrades and retirements with minimal SLO perturbation by: 1) streaming hot-key metadata and KV-prefetch manifests to target hosts, 2) performing background KV fetch & cache warm-up, 3) gradually shifting traffic via fine-grained connection handover, and 4) validating correctness before final decommission. This ticket covers design, simulation, implementation hooks in runtime, autoscaler interactions, and a staged rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Can retire a host in production with no more than 3% P95 latency increase across sampled routes during the maintenance window
Replacement hosts receive at least 80% of the retiring host's hot-key set in cache before they handle steady-state traffic for that key range
No dropped or failed requests attributable to missing KV state during the reintegration flow in canary tests
Metrics and tracing show graceful handover events and the reintegration step is visible in Console rollout traces
Automated rollback triggers if latency or error rate exceeds configured thresholds during rollout
design_notes: We avoid a global pause by using per-shard handover epochs; each shard negotiates a transfer window with peers via the control plane
State ferry consists of two parts: (A) compact hot-key manifest (small) and (B) prioritized prefetch list (larger, used to warm cache asynchronously)
Control-plane handshake includes versioned manifest checksum to detect divergence and ensure idempotent retries
Autoscaler integration: coordinate with autoscaler to provision replacement capacity ahead of heavy fetches and to avoid autoscale churn during warm-up
Fallback behavior: if KV warm-up fails for a shard, route that shard's traffic to a soft-fallback model variant with higher latency budget while retrying warm-up
implementation_tasks: Add control-plane RPCs for 'ferry_start', 'ferry_chunk', 'ferry_complete' with retry/idempotency semantics
Implement manifest generator in retiring host that computes hot-key set using recent access histogram
Build async prefetch worker on replacement hosts that consumes manifest and populates KV cache with priority ordering
Expose per-shard handover state in runtime tracing and Console events
Update autoscaler to accept 'handshake_reserved' flag so provision happens before ferry starts
Create health-check hooks: pre-ready, warm-ready, and live-ready to gate traffic shift
Create simulation harness to run synthetic workloads and validate warm-up timing under different TTFB profiles
milestones: M3 - Runtime prefetch worker and tracing (2025-03-28)
rollout_plan: Alpha: run in infra test cluster with synthetic traffic; validate metrics and tracing
Beta: enable for non-critical tenant fleet with small percentage of host retirements
Canary: 1% of production fleet with strict SLO thresholds and automated rollback
Gradual ramp: increase to 10% then 50% over successive maintenance cycles while monitoring
Full: default for scheduled retirements once stable metrics confirmed
metrics: per-shard cache fill ratio before/after ferry
P50/P95/P99 latency delta during ferry windows (by route)
error-rate delta attributable to missing state
qa_plan: Unit tests for manifest generation and chunking logic
Integration tests for control-plane RPC idempotency and retry scenarios
Chaos test: random ferry interruption and resumption with shard reconciliation
Load test: synthetic workload to validate prefetch throughput and autoscaler behavior
End-to-end canary with telemetry assertions and automated rollback script
